city.tagline: The lake, the ravines, and a free museum night most weeks
city.heroDescription: Toronto's best days out are often its cheapest: a ferry to the Islands, a walk through the ravines, a market in Kensington, a free night at a major museum. Listings here come from the City of Toronto's open data and from local curators, and events update from the City's festivals feed.

drop: Woodbine Shopping Centre and Fantasy Fair
St. Lawrence Market and Market Gallery

Textile Museum of Canada: Small admission fee. Check the website.
Toronto Railway Museum: Small admission fee. Check the website.
Steam Whistle Brewery: Free to visit. Paid tours and tastings.
Centreville Amusement Park: Free to enter. Pay for rides.
TIFF Bell Lightbox: Free to enter. Pay per film.

places.name: High Park
places.description: Toronto's biggest park: forest trails, Grenadier Pond, a free zoo, and cherry blossoms every spring.

places.name: Toronto Island Park
places.costNote: Ferry is $9.57 round trip for adults. The park itself is free.
places.description: A short ferry ride to beaches, car-free paths, and the best skyline view in the city.

places.name: Evergreen Brick Works
places.costNote: Free to visit. Some workshops are paid.
places.description: A former brickyard turned ravine park, with trails, ponds, and a weekend farmers' market.

places.name: Scarborough Bluffs at Bluffer's Park
places.description: White cliffs over Lake Ontario, with a sandy Blue Flag beach and picnic spots at the base.

places.name: Woodbine Beach and the Boardwalk
places.description: A long sandy beach and boardwalk in the east end, busy all summer and lovely on a winter walk.

places.name: Tommy Thompson Park
places.description: A wild peninsula built from construction rubble, now one of the best spots in the city for birds and bike rides.

places.name: Rouge National Urban Park
places.description: Canada's first national urban park, with marshes, forest trails, and no entry fee.

places.name: West Toronto Railpath
places.description: A car-free path along the rail corridor through the west end, lined with murals and gardens.

places.name: The Bentway
places.description: Public space under the Gardiner Expressway with art, events, and a winter skating trail.
places.seasonNote: Skate trail in winter. Check the website for dates.

places.name: Nathan Phillips Square Rink
places.costNote: Free to skate. Rentals cost extra.
places.description: Skate free under the arches in front of City Hall, usually from late November.

places.name: Riverdale Farm
places.description: A working farm in Cabbagetown with cows, pigs, and goats, free for everyone.

places.name: Allan Gardens Conservatory
places.description: A warm Victorian glasshouse full of palms and cactus, free to walk through on the coldest day of the year.

places.name: Toronto Music Garden
places.description: A waterfront garden designed around a Bach cello suite, with free concerts in summer.

places.name: Toronto Reference Library
places.hours: Mon to Fri 9am to 8:30pm; Sat 9am to 5pm; Sun 1:30pm to 5pm
places.description: Five floors around a soaring atrium, with free wifi, quiet desks, and exhibits.

places.name: Museum + Arts Pass at the library
places.costNote: Free with a Toronto Public Library card.
places.description: Borrow free family passes to the ROM, AGO, zoo, and more with your library card.

places.name: Fair Pass Transit Discount
places.description: Discounted TTC fares for Torontonians on low incomes.

places.name: Free Tax Clinics
places.description: Volunteers file simple tax returns for free if you have a modest income.

places.name: Credit Canada
places.costNote: Free counselling. Debt programs may have fees.
places.description: Free, confidential help with debt and budgeting from a non-profit credit counsellor.

places.name: WoodGreen Community Services
places.description: Job help, newcomer services, and free programs across east Toronto.

places.name: 211 Toronto
places.description: Call or text 211 to find any community service in the city, in over 150 languages.

places.name: The 519
places.description: A Church-Wellesley community centre with free programs and drop-ins for 2SLGBTQ+ people.

places.name: Scadding Court Community Centre
places.costNote: Many programs are free. Some have a fee.
places.description: A downtown community centre with a pool, programs, and a shipping-container market.

places.name: Access Alliance
places.description: Free health care and settlement help for newcomers and refugees.

places.name: Toronto Event Generator
places.description: A weekly email of hands-on events around the city where you can actually meet people.

places.name: Snakes & Lattes Annex
places.costNote: Game fee per person, plus food and drinks.
places.description: A board game cafe with thousands of games and staff who will teach you the rules.

places.name: Gerstein Crisis Centre
places.description: A 24-hour mental health crisis line for adults in Toronto.

places.name: 9-8-8 Suicide Crisis Helpline
places.description: Call or text 988 any time to reach a trained responder.

places.name: Art Gallery of Ontario
places.costNote: Free first Wednesday nights. Check the website for prices and youth passes.
places.description: One of North America's great art museums, with a free night on the first Wednesday of the month.

places.name: Royal Ontario Museum
places.costNote: Check the website for prices and the free main floor.
places.description: Dinosaurs, world cultures, and natural history under the Crystal.

places.name: Gardiner Museum
places.costNote: Free Wednesdays after 4pm.
places.hours: Mon to Fri 10am to 6pm; Sat to Sun 10am to 5pm
places.description: A small, lovely museum of ceramics, free on Wednesday evenings.

places.name: Aga Khan Museum
places.costNote: Free Wednesdays, 4 to 8pm.
places.hours: Tue 10am to 5:30pm; Wed 10am to 8pm; Thu to Sun 10am to 5:30pm; closed Mon
places.description: Islamic art and culture in a striking building with reflecting pools outside.

places.name: Bata Shoe Museum
places.costNote: $16 for adults. Free on Sundays.
places.hours: Mon to Sat 10am to 5pm; Sun 12pm to 5pm
places.description: Thousands of years of footwear, and much more fun than it sounds. Free on Sundays.

places.name: MOCA Toronto
places.costNote: Free on the first Sunday of the month.
places.description: Contemporary art in a converted factory, free on the first Sunday of each month.

places.name: Graffiti Alley
places.description: Three blocks of murals behind Queen Street West, always open and always changing.

places.name: Kensington Market
places.costNote: Free to wander. Cheap eats everywhere.
places.description: Toronto's most colourful few blocks: cheap eats, vintage shops, and cheese mongers in old Victorian houses.

places.name: St. Lawrence Market
places.costNote: Free to browse.
places.description: A huge historic food hall downtown, known for peameal bacon sandwiches.

places.name: The Stop Community Food Centre
places.description: Free community meals, a food bank, and cooking programs in the west end.

places.name: Daily Bread Food Bank
places.description: Find your nearest food bank across the city with no paperwork fuss.

places.name: Moonbean Coffee
places.costNote: A coffee runs a few dollars.
places.description: A long-running Kensington Market coffee shop that roasts its own beans, with a small back patio.

places.name: Dark Horse Espresso, Spadina
places.costNote: A coffee runs a few dollars.
places.description: A big, bright Toronto coffee shop on Spadina with long tables, good for a slow morning.

places.name: Pilot Coffee Roasters
places.costNote: A coffee runs a few dollars.
places.description: The cafe at a well-known Toronto roaster's East York roastery.

places.name: Rooster Coffee House
places.description: A neighbourhood coffee shop across from Riverdale Park, with the skyline a short walk away.

places.name: Balzac's Coffee, Distillery District
places.description: Coffee in a two-storey Victorian pump house in the Distillery District.

places.name: Jimmy's Coffee, Kensington
places.description: A relaxed Kensington cafe with a patio that is hard to leave.

places.name: Type Books
places.costNote: Free to browse.
places.description: An independent bookstore across from Trinity Bellwoods.

places.name: Courage My Love
places.description: A Kensington institution for vintage clothes, beads, and buttons at fair prices.

places.name: Double Take Thrift Store
places.description: A low-priced thrift store run by Yonge Street Mission, with proceeds going to its programs.

places.name: Value Village, Bloor
places.description: A big, reliable thrift store near Ossington station.

places.name: Free Concerts at the Opera House
places.description: Free noon-hour concerts in the glass lobby of the Four Seasons Centre, usually on weekdays.
places.seasonNote: Runs fall to spring. Check the schedule.

places.name: The Rex Hotel Jazz & Blues Bar
places.costNote: Many sets are free or a small cover.
places.description: Toronto's long-running jazz bar, with live sets most days of the week.
